title: Cipher and Ghost
premise: Silas Vane, a crash investigator haunted by the unexplained death of his family in row twelve, is approached by a stranger who claims Silas once saved her life — a favor he never performed, and one she now repays by dragging him into an intelligence operation to extract Nadia Reiss, a defector carrying proof that the summit's host government engineered the crash that killed his family. As Silas and a ragtag extraction team — a disgraced pilot, a forger, and the stranger, Mara — move Nadia across borders, they discover she may be deliberate bait in a trap meant to flush out dissenters before the summit. Betrayed from within and hunted by the man who ordered row twelve, Silas must choose between exposing the truth at the summit or saving the found family he never expected to have. In the end, Silas trades his polished lie for the raw truth broadcast to the delegates, destroys the architect's inheritance of power, and walks away with Mara and Nadia — alive, unproven, and finally unpacked.
about_author: Felix Ashgrove is the pen name of a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade reading black-box transcripts before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about ordinary people forced to audit their own pasts, and lives somewhere with good train connections and bad weather.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Silas Vane's POV. At a crash site in fog, Silas reconstructs wreckage with clinical precision while privately fixating on row twelve — where his family died three years ago. He keeps a go-bag in his trunk and a rehearsed story about being 'over it.' Emotional beat: grief disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: A woman named Mara intercepts Silas outside his office, thanking him for saving her life in Prague — an event he has no memory of. She leaves a burner phone and a warning: interest is owed. POV: Silas. Beat: unease; the first crack in his controlled world.

chapters.title: Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Silas investigates the Prague claim through flight manifests and finds his name forged onto a passenger list — someone built him a false history. His apartment shows signs of entry, nothing taken. POV: Silas. Beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve; he packs the go-bag properly for the first time.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: The burner rings. A handler called Corvus offers Silas a role extracting defector Nadia Reiss, hinting that files she carries mention row twelve. Refusal means the forged history becomes criminal evidence against him. POV: Silas. Beat: coercion dressed as opportunity.

chapters.title: The Defector
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In a safehouse outside Riga, we meet Nadia Reiss — brilliant, brittle, convinced she's already dead. Mara briefs the team: pilot Dov Hale, grounded after a scandal; forger Ilsa Brandt. Beat: found-family seeds planted among strangers with nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: Recruitment
chapters.summary: Silas meets the team and hates them all on sight. Dov mocks his luggage; Ilsa reads his forged documents like a diary. Nadia studies him too long and says, 'You look like a man auditing himself.' POV: Silas. Beat: friction masking mutual recognition.

chapters.title: Manifest
chapters.summary: Silas decrypts part of Nadia's cargo: a maintenance log proving Flight 4471's tail section was tampered with — and a codename, GARDENER, belonging to someone inside the summit's host delegation. POV: Silas. Beat: hope curdling into rage; the crash was murder.

chapters.title: Crossing the Narva
chapters.summary: The extraction begins. Border crossing goes wrong when a checkpoint guard recognizes Ilsa's forgery batch. Dov improvises a diversion; Mara kills for the first time in years and doesn't flinch. POV: Mara. Beat: the team bonds under fire; Silas sees Mara clearly for the first time.

chapters.title: What Nadia Knows
chapters.summary: Nadia reveals she was the analyst who flagged the tampering and was disavowed — but admits she can't verify which copy of her files is real. 'They let me take both,' she says. POV: Nadia. Beat: doubt enters the mission; is she courier or bait?

chapters.title: GARDENER
chapters.summary: Silas traces GARDENER to Deputy Minister Aris Kessler, the summit's security architect — a man whose career was built on the tragedy Silas survived. Flashback to row twelve's funeral. POV: Silas. Beat: vengeance crystallizing into obsession.

chapters.title: Safe House Rules
chapters.summary: A quiet chapter: hiding in a Vilnius basement, the team cooks, bickers, plays cards. Ilsa teaches Nadia card tricks; Dov tells the truth about his scandal. POV: Dov. Beat: warmth — the found family forming, making what comes next hurt more.

chapters.title: The Second Copy
chapters.summary: Ilsa discovers Nadia's two file sets differ in one detail: the second implicates Mara's old unit. Confrontation. Mara admits she ran the Prague op that supposedly saved her own cover — the favor was manufactured. POV: Ilsa. Beat: betrayal tremor; trust fractures.

chapters.title: Prague, Reconstructed
chapters.summary: Silas forces Mara to walk him through the fabricated rescue. She confesses she chose him because his grief made him predictable — then admits she kept watching because it stopped being an assignment. POV: Mara. Beat: raw honesty; something real inside the lie.

chapters.title: Corvus Calls
chapters.summary: The handler orders the team to deliver Nadia to a summit-adjacent handoff point — exactly the trap pattern Nadia predicted. Silas realizes Corvus wants them flushed into the open. POV: Silas. Beat: the mission revealed as a hunt.

chapters.title: Split Decision
chapters.summary: Vote: obey Corvus or go dark. Dov votes dark; Ilsa wavers; Nadia offers to surrender herself as decoy. Mara overrules everyone: they split — decoy convoy, real route north. POV: Mara. Beat: leadership under moral weight.

chapters.title: Decoy
chapters.summary: Ilsa drives the decoy van wearing Nadia's coat. The ambush comes early and professional; she survives by driving into a frozen canal. POV: Ilsa. Beat: terror and gallows humor; cost made visible.

chapters.title: Kessler's Garden
chapters.summary: Kessler's POV. We see the antagonist tending literal roses, reviewing photos of Silas's team. He authorized row twelve to protect an arms pipeline; the summit will legitimize it. Beat: chilling banality; power as horticulture — pruning people.

chapters.title: Northbound
chapters.summary: The real group moves by fishing boat through the archipelago. Dov flies them off a strip carved from ice. Silas and Nadia talk about inheritance — what our dead leave us besides grief. POV: Silas. Beat: quiet bonding; stakes humanized.

chapters.title: The Mole
chapters.summary: Their safe arrival is known within hours. Someone transmitted. Suspicion circles Nadia — until Silas realizes the leak pattern matches Corvus's own channel. They were never trusted; they were tracked. POV: Nadia. Beat: dread; no clean allies.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Firelight
chapters.summary: Trapped in a lighthouse, the team interrogates each other gently, brutally. Old wounds surface: Dov's scandal, Ilsa's prison years, Mara's unit. Nadia watches and says they're the first honest people she's met. POV: rotating vignettes. Beat: catharsis; family forged in suspicion.

chapters.title: Corvus Unmasked
chapters.summary: Silas baits Corvus with false coordinates and traces the response: Corvus is Kessler's intelligence chief — and the voice who once ordered the row-twelve maintenance falsification. POV: Silas. Beat: the personal and political merge into one enemy.

chapters.title: Bait Confirmed
chapters.summary: Nadia confirms it herself: Kessler let her defect. Her files are the lure to discredit every dissident voice before the summit ratifies the pipeline treaty. 'I'm the gift,' she says, 'wrapped in my own autopsy.' POV: Nadia. Beat: despair transformed into strategy.

chapters.title: The Counterfeit Truth
chapters.summary: Plan forms: if Nadia is bait, use her. Deliver a doctored version of the files to Kessler while the authentic log goes to delegates through Ilsa's forgery network. POV: Ilsa. Beat: agency reclaimed; victims become authors.

chapters.title: Summit City
chapters.summary: Infiltration of the capital. Kessler's security state rendered in unsettling detail — cheerful banners, facial-recognition kiosks, children's choirs rehearsing anthems. POV: Silas. Beat: oppression wearing a festival mask.

chapters.title: Old Contacts
chapters.summary: Dov calls in a debt with a hangar owner who owes him a life; they gain access to summit airside. The contact warns: Kessler knows an extraction team is in-country. POV: Dov. Beat: borrowed time, borrowed loyalty.

chapters.title: Mara's Unit
chapters.summary: Mara's former commander offers her reinstatement if she delivers Nadia and Silas. She records the offer instead. POV: Mara. Beat: choosing the new family over the old institution; power's price quoted aloud.

chapters.title: Handoff
chapters.summary: The doctored files reach Kessler via a cutout. He celebrates, ordering the trap sprung at the cultural gala — where 'the defector' will be publicly arrested. POV: Kessler. Beat: dramatic irony tightening like a garrote.

chapters.title: Gala
chapters.summary: Silas, in a stolen delegate's suit, watches Kessler work the room. Nadia, supposed to be hidden, appears anyway — insisting the plan needs her face in the crowd. POV: Silas. Beat: dread and admiration; control slipping.

chapters.title: Sprung
chapters.summary: The trap closes — but on Kessler's own men, fed false locations. Chaos in the gala hall; Mara extracts Nadia through service corridors while Silas confronts Corvus face to face. POV: Mara. Beat: adrenaline; the hunters hunted.

chapters.title: Corvus
chapters.summary: Silas and Corvus fight in a archive corridor full of shredded documents. Silas wins but learns the final secret: the original order for row twelve came not from Kessler but from Kessler's patron — the summit's chairwoman. POV: Silas. Beat: the ceiling of corruption rises.

chapters.title: Chairwoman
chapters.summary: Flashback interleave: the chairwoman inherited the arms empire from her father and pruned witnesses for thirty years, including Silas's family, who were collateral in a cleanup. POV: Chairwoman. Beat: inheritance as horror; power reproducing itself.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ilsa's network pushes the authentic maintenance log to delegate devices mid-session. The summit fractures; delegations walk out; the treaty dies on the floor. POV: Ilsa. Beat: truth as detonation.

chapters.title: Siege
chapters.summary: Kessler, exposed, tries to burn everything: seize Nadia, kill the team, blame terrorists. The city locks down around the safehouse. POV: Nadia. Beat: cornered-animal tension.

chapters.title: Airside
chapters.summary: Escape attempt via Dov's borrowed plane. Checkpoint standoff; the hangar owner returns to settle his debt, buying them ninety seconds with his body. POV: Dov. Beat: sacrifice; debts paid in blood.

chapters.title: Kessler's Fall
chapters.summary: Kessler corners them on the runway — and is undone by his own protégé, who trades him to investigators for immunity. Power devours its heir. POV: Silas. Beat: poetic justice, coldly delivered.

chapters.title: Row Twelve, Answered
chapters.summary: Silas finally reads the full crash report alone. He speaks his family's names aloud at the site fence and leaves the go-bag there — packed, no longer needed. POV: Silas. Beat: grief given an answer; mourning allowed to begin.

chapters.title: The Chairwoman's Silence
chapters.summary: The chairwoman isn't prosecuted — too insulated — but the broadcast ends her empire's future; the inheritance dies with her reputation. She sends Silas one message: 'You audited me well.' POV: Chairwoman. Beat: imperfect justice, honestly rendered.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Epilogue-adjacent: months later, a rented house near the sea. Dov flies crop dusters, Ilsa teaches art restoration (legally), Nadia testifies remotely. Mara and Silas plant a garden neither knows how to tend. POV: Mara. Beat: domestic peace earned, still slightly unbelievable.

chapters.title: The Stranger Returns
chapters.summary: Final beat: a stranger knocks, thanking Silas for a favor he never performed — again. This time, Silas laughs, invites her in, and asks how much interest. POV: Silas. Beat: the cycle acknowledged; family open to the next lost soul.

chapters.title: Cipher and Ghost
chapters.summary: Coda in Nadia's voice: she archives everything — the cipher of files, the ghosts of row twelve — into a memorial database anyone can read. 'Truth inherited is the only kind that lasts.' POV: Nadia. Beat: thematic resolution; memory as legacy.
